findings.finding: The opening revision-note banner at the top of design.md still says 'this is the second revision pass' and only names round 2 by name, but the document now contains five 'Responses to design review findings' resolution tables (rounds 1-5), the latest appended at the end. The banner is stale relative to the document's actual revision history, which could mislead a fresh reader about how many review cycles have occurred.
findings.fix: Update the banner to: "Revision note: this document has gone through five revision passes, each addressing the design review that followed the prior pass. Resolution logs for all five rounds are kept at the end of this document under 'Responses to design review findings (round N)'."

findings.finding: The store_packet code sample added for the R5-M1 fix calls cur.execute("BEGIN") explicitly before the INSERTs and _conn.commit()/_conn.rollback() afterward, but the design never states what isolation_level the module-level connection is opened with. Verified against CPython's actual Modules/_sqlite/cursor.c that this shape is safe regardless (sqlite3's implicit-transaction-before-DML logic only triggers when no transaction is already open, which is no longer true once the explicit BEGIN has run), but the design doesn't say so, leaving an implementer who knows sqlite3's docs on mixing manual BEGIN with implicit transactions to wonder whether an explicit isolation_level= argument is needed.
findings.fix: Add one clause to the _conn construction description: "_conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH, check_same_thread=False) -- isolation_level is left at its default; the explicit cur.execute('BEGIN') in each write function works correctly regardless, because sqlite3's implicit-transaction-before-DML logic only triggers when no transaction is already open, which is no longer the case once BEGIN has executed."
